tools.name: sonarr-series-lookup
tools.description: START HERE for any TV download request: 'download <show>', 'download <show> S02E05', 'get/grab the latest episode of <show>', 'download a torrent/file' for a series. Searches TheTVDB (via Sonarr) by name and reports inLibrary per match. Then: inLibrary=true -> sonarr-episodes to find the episode id -> sonarr-run-command EpisodeSearch (Sonarr picks a release matching the quality profile and sends it to qBittorrent), or sonarr-releases + sonarr-grab-release when the user named a specific release. inLibrary=false -> sonarr-quality-profiles + sonarr-root-folders -> sonarr-series-add with searchForMissingEpisodes. Not sure whether <x> is a show or a movie? Try radarr-movie-lookup too.
tools.filter: [.[] | {id, tvdbId, title, year, status, network, seasons: (.seasons|length), inLibrary: ((.id // 0) > 0), overview: (.overview // "" | .[0:200])}]

tools.name: sonarr-series-list
tools.description: Every series in the Sonarr library with per-season episode/file counts. Prefer sonarr-series-lookup or sonarr-series-get when you already know the series.
tools.filter: [.[] | {id, title, year, status, monitored, network, qualityProfileId, path, nextAiring, seasons: [.seasons[] | {seasonNumber, monitored, episodes: .statistics.episodeCount, files: .statistics.episodeFileCount}]}]

tools.name: sonarr-series-get
tools.description: One library series by its Sonarr id, including seasons, monitoring flags, quality profile and root folder.
tools.filter: {id, tvdbId, title, year, status, monitored, network, qualityProfileId, rootFolderPath, path, nextAiring, previousAiring, seasons: [.seasons[] | {seasonNumber, monitored, episodes: .statistics.episodeCount, files: .statistics.episodeFileCount, sizeOnDisk: .statistics.sizeOnDisk}]}

tools.name: sonarr-episodes
tools.description: Episodes of a series (optionally one season): ids, air dates, whether a file exists, monitored flag. Episode ids are what sonarr-run-command EpisodeSearch needs.
tools.filter: [.[] | {id, seasonNumber, episodeNumber, title, airDateUtc, hasFile, monitored, episodeFileId}]

tools.name: sonarr-wanted-missing
tools.description: Monitored episodes that have aired but have no file, newest first. Paged.
tools.filter: {page, pageSize, totalRecords, records: [.records[] | {id, seriesId, series: .series.title, seasonNumber, episodeNumber, title, airDateUtc, monitored}]}

tools.name: sonarr-queue
tools.description: Current download queue with status, progress and problems. An item with trackedDownloadState=importPending plus statusMessages (e.g. 'Found executable file', 'Invalid video file', 'No files eligible for import') is STUCK: it downloaded but Sonarr refuses to import it. Each item has an id for sonarr-queue-remove. Two entries for the same episode means duplicate downloads: keep the one further along (or the one the user asked for) and sonarr-queue-remove the other with blocklist=false.
tools.filter: {totalRecords, records: [.records[] | {id, seriesId, series: .series.title, seasonNumber: .episode.seasonNumber, episodeNumber: .episode.episodeNumber, episodeId, title, status, trackedDownloadStatus, trackedDownloadState, size, sizeleft, timeleft, protocol, downloadClient, indexer, errorMessage, statusMessages: [.statusMessages[]? | .messages[]?]}]}

tools.name: sonarr-queue-remove
tools.description: Remove one queue item, and with removeFromClient=true also remove the torrent from qBittorrent; blocklist=true stops Sonarr grabbing that release again. Do this FIRST whenever a download is stuck, bad, an exe, won't import, or the user wants 'a better copy': remove with removeFromClient=true and blocklist=true, THEN search again (sonarr-run-command EpisodeSearch) or grab a DIFFERENT release via sonarr-releases + sonarr-grab-release. Skipping this step makes the next grab fail, because qBittorrent already has the torrent.

removeFromClient.description: Also remove the torrent from qBittorrent

blocklist.description: Blocklist this release so it is not grabbed again

tools.name: sonarr-history
tools.description: Recent grab/import/removal/failure events, newest first. Useful for 'what happened to X' questions.
tools.filter: {totalRecords, records: [.records[] | {id, date, eventType, seriesId, series: .series.title, seasonNumber: .episode.seasonNumber, episodeNumber: .episode.episodeNumber, sourceTitle, quality: .quality.quality.name, indexer: .data.indexer, downloadClient: .data.downloadClient, reason: .data.reason}]}

tools.name: sonarr-calendar
tools.description: Episodes airing in a date range (upcoming and recent), with whether each already has a file.
tools.filter: [.[] | {id, seriesId, series: .series.title, seasonNumber, episodeNumber, title, airDateUtc, hasFile, monitored}]

tools.name: sonarr-run-command
tools.description: Trigger a Sonarr task; this is how 'download <episode>' is normally fulfilled once the episode id is known (EpisodeSearch): Sonarr searches the indexers, applies the quality profile and sends the best release to qBittorrent. name is one of: EpisodeSearch (episodeIds: [..]), SeriesSearch (seriesId), SeasonSearch (seriesId, seasonNumber), MissingEpisodeSearch (all missing), RefreshSeries (seriesId, optional), RssSync. Returns the queued command; poll sonarr-commands, then sonarr-queue to confirm a grab. If nothing was grabbed, sonarr-releases shows why. Check sonarr-queue first: if the episode is already downloading, a new search is pointless.
tools.filter: {id, name, status, queued, message}

tools.name: sonarr-releases
tools.description: Manual search: every release the indexers return for one episode, with Sonarr's verdict (approved) and rejection reasons (wrong quality for profile, too small, already in queue...). Use when the user asks to download a SPECIFIC release/torrent by name (e.g. 'download Lanterns S01E06 1080p WEB H264 CAKES'), or to see why an automatic search grabbed nothing. Match the wanted title, then pass its guid + indexerId to sonarr-grab-release. When replacing a bad download, never pick the release that is already in the queue (same title as the stuck item, or rejection 'already in queue'); pick a different release group. SIZE POLICY when choosing which release to grab: prefer 2-3 GB; if nothing suitable is in that range, up to 5 GB is fine; anything ABOVE 5 GB needs the user's explicit approval before grabbing - show the title and size and ask. Among candidates in range prefer more seeders and a well-known release group, and skip anything with rejections about executables or blocklist.

episodeId.description: Episode id from sonarr-episodes or sonarr-wanted-missing

tools.filter: [.[] | {guid, indexerId, indexer, title, size, sizeGB: ((.size / 1073741824 * 10 | round) / 10), seeders, leechers, age, publishDate, protocol, quality: .quality.quality.name, customFormatScore, approved, rejections}]

tools.name: sonarr-grab-release
tools.description: Download one specific release from sonarr-releases, bypassing quality-profile rejections (not size/blocklist ones). Sends it to qBittorrent and tracks it in sonarr-queue. BEFORE calling: check sonarr-queue; if a healthy copy of this episode is already downloading (no statusMessages), do not start a second one unless the user explicitly wants it replaced, and then sonarr-queue-remove the old one first. A rejection reading 'Release in queue already meets cutoff' means exactly that: a good copy is already in the queue, so report it instead of grabbing. If the call fails with 'Download client failed to add torrent', that torrent is already in qBittorrent (usually the stuck one): sonarr-queue-remove it with removeFromClient=true, blocklist=true, then grab a DIFFERENT release. A normal (non-error) result means the grab succeeded, whatever the release's earlier approved/rejections flags said; confirm with sonarr-queue and tell the user what was grabbed. SIZE POLICY when choosing which release to grab: prefer 2-3 GB; if nothing suitable is in that range, up to 5 GB is fine; anything ABOVE 5 GB needs the user's explicit approval before grabbing - show the title and size and ask. Among candidates in range prefer more seeders and a well-known release group, and skip anything with rejections about executables or blocklist.
tools.filter: {grabbed: true, title, indexer, size, quality: .quality.quality.name}

tools.name: sonarr-commands
tools.description: Status of recently queued Sonarr commands (searches, refreshes): queued / started / completed / failed.
tools.filter: [.[] | {id, name, status, queued, started, ended, message}]

tools.name: sonarr-quality-profiles
tools.description: Quality profiles (id + name), needed for sonarr-series-add.
tools.filter: [.[] | {id, name}]

tools.name: sonarr-release-profiles
tools.description: List release profiles: per-profile required terms and ignored terms (a release whose TITLE contains an ignored term is rejected before it is sent to qBittorrent). Read-only, changes nothing. This is the simplest place to block a term such as .exe.
tools.filter: [.[] | {id, name, enabled, required, ignored, indexerId, tags}]

tools.name: sonarr-release-profile-add
tools.description: Create a release profile. To block executables by title, pass ignored: [".exe"] with enabled true and indexerId 0 (all indexers). Terms are matched case-insensitively against the release title; prefix a term with /regex/ for a regular expression. Returns the created profile.

required.description: Title must contain at least one of these (leave empty for none)

ignored.description: Title must contain NONE of these, e.g. [".exe"]

tools.filter: {id, name, enabled, required, ignored, indexerId}

tools.name: sonarr-release-profile-edit
tools.description: Replace one release profile by id. Send the WHOLE profile as it should end up: read it first with sonarr-release-profiles, add or remove terms, then send every field back (name, enabled, required, ignored, indexerId, tags). Use this to add .exe to an existing profile rather than making a second one.
tools.filter: {id, name, enabled, required, ignored, indexerId}

tools.name: sonarr-release-profile-remove
tools.description: Permanently remove a release profile by id. Destructive: confirm with the user first, and prefer sonarr-release-profile-edit when the goal is only to take one term out.

tools.name: sonarr-custom-formats
tools.description: List custom formats and the specifications inside each one (what a format matches). Read-only. Custom formats only change SCORING: a format scores points on a quality profile, and a release is refused when its total falls below that profile minFormatScore. See sonarr-quality-profile-scoring.
tools.filter: [.[] | {id, name, includeCustomFormatWhenRenaming, specifications: [.specifications[] | {name, implementation, negate, required, value: (.fields[]? | select(.name == "value") | .value)}]}]

tools.name: sonarr-custom-format-schema
tools.description: The specification types a custom format can use on this Sonarr, with the fields each one takes (ReleaseTitleSpecification, SizeSpecification, ReleaseGroupSpecification, ResolutionSpecification, SourceSpecification, LanguageSpecification, ReleaseTypeSpecification, IndexerFlagSpecification). Read-only. Check here before building a format.
tools.filter: [.[] | {implementation, implementationName, fields: [.fields[]? | {name, label, type}]}]

tools.name: sonarr-custom-format-add
tools.description: Create a custom format. specifications is a list; for a title match use implementation ReleaseTitleSpecification with fields [{name: value, value: <regex>}], e.g. value "\\.exe" to match a title containing .exe. Creating the format alone changes nothing: give it a negative score on each quality profile with sonarr-quality-profile-scoring-edit, and set that profile minFormatScore above the negative total so matching releases are refused.
tools.filter: {id, name, specifications: [.specifications[] | {name, implementation, negate, required}]}

tools.name: sonarr-custom-format-edit
tools.description: Replace one custom format by id. Read it with sonarr-custom-formats first and send the whole object back (id, name, includeCustomFormatWhenRenaming, specifications).
tools.filter: {id, name, specifications: [.specifications[] | {name, implementation, negate, required}]}

tools.name: sonarr-custom-format-remove
tools.description: Permanently remove a custom format by id, and with it every score it carries on the quality profiles. Destructive: confirm with the user first.

tools.name: sonarr-quality-profile-scoring
tools.description: Read one quality profile in full, including formatItems (the score each custom format carries here), minFormatScore (a release scoring below this is refused), cutoffFormatScore and minUpgradeFormatScore. Read-only. Everything here is needed to build the body for sonarr-quality-profile-scoring-edit.

tools.name: sonarr-quality-profile-scoring-edit
tools.description: Replace one quality profile by id, which is how a custom format gets its score. Read the profile with sonarr-quality-profile-scoring, change only formatItems (set score to -10000 on the format to block) and minFormatScore (e.g. -100, so anything carrying the -10000 is refused), then send back EVERY field unchanged: name, upgradeAllowed, cutoff, items, minFormatScore, cutoffFormatScore, minUpgradeFormatScore, formatItems. Omitting items or cutoff will damage the profile, so never send a partial body.
tools.filter: {id, name, minFormatScore, cutoffFormatScore, formatItems: [.formatItems[] | select(.score != 0) | {format, name, score}]}

tools.name: sonarr-root-folders
tools.description: Root folders (path + free space), needed for sonarr-series-add.
tools.filter: [.[] | {id, path, freeSpace, accessible}]

tools.name: sonarr-series-add
tools.description: Add a series to the library and optionally start downloading. Use for 'download <show>' when sonarr-series-lookup says inLibrary=false. tvdbId/title from the lookup, qualityProfileId from sonarr-quality-profiles, rootFolderPath from sonarr-root-folders; set addOptions.searchForMissingEpisodes=true to start downloads immediately.

addOptions.description: e.g. {"monitor": "all", "searchForMissingEpisodes": true}. monitor: all | future | missing | existing | firstSeason | latestSeason | none

tools.filter: {id, tvdbId, title, year, monitored, path, qualityProfileId}

tools.name: sonarr-health
tools.description: Sonarr health warnings/errors (indexer failures, download client unreachable, root folder missing...). Empty list = healthy.

tools.name: sonarr-system-status
tools.description: Sonarr version, uptime/start time, OS and paths.
